title: Welcoming new students
context_es: La dirección de tu escuela internacional de idiomas quiere mejorar la acogida de los alumnos nuevos y pide propuestas a los estudiantes.
prompt_en:
The director of the international language school where you study wants to improve the way new students from other countries are welcomed during their first weeks. Students have been invited to send in proposals.

Write a proposal in which you outline the difficulties new students face, suggest two or three ways of helping them and explain how your ideas would benefit the school as a whole.
points: outline the difficulties new students face
suggest two or three ways of helping them
explain how your ideas would benefit the school
useful_language: The purpose of this proposal is to …
Having spoken to a number of students, I have identified …
This would be inexpensive to produce.
Were these measures to be adopted, …
I hope these suggestions will be given serious consideration.
tips_es: Una propuesta mira al futuro y quiere convencer: describe el problema en poco espacio y dedica el resto a soluciones concretas.
Secciones con título, como en un informe, y lenguaje de sugerencia: *I would suggest* + -ing, *the school could…*
No olvides el beneficio para quien decide: es lo que hace persuasiva una propuesta.
model_answer:
Introduction

The purpose of this proposal is to outline the difficulties that new international students experience during their first weeks at the school and to suggest practical ways of making their arrival easier.

Current difficulties

Having spoken to a number of students who joined last term, I have identified two main problems. Firstly, many newcomers find it hard to deal with practical matters such as opening a bank account or registering with a doctor, since the information is scattered and available only in English. Secondly, several students reported feeling isolated, as friendships within classes had already been formed before they arrived.

Recommendations

I would suggest introducing a mentoring scheme in which each new student is paired with a volunteer who has been at the school for at least a term. Mentors could meet their partners once a week and answer everyday questions.

In addition, the school could publish a short welcome guide, translated into the most common languages, covering transport, health care and accommodation. This would be inexpensive to produce and could be updated every year.

Finally, a social evening in the first week of each term would give newcomers the chance to meet people outside their own class.

Benefits

Were these measures to be adopted, new students would settle in more quickly and would therefore make faster progress. Moreover, satisfied students are far more likely to recommend the school to others, which would enhance its reputation abroad.

Conclusion

I am confident that these suggestions could be implemented cheaply, and I hope they will be given serious consideration.
